extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal financial assistance (K-12 schools and postsecondary institutions), Title IX coordinators, school administrators, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on §106.44(c) emergency removals under Title IX: substantive threshold for removal, required individualized safety/risk analysis, interaction with supportive measures and disability laws, and post-removal notice and challenge requirements for respondents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency removal threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency removal under §106.44(c) is permissible only where there is an immediate threat to the physical health or safety of any student or other individual arising from the allegations of sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a high threshold intended to restrict emergency removals to genuine emergencies. The provision was revised to refer to the physical health or safety of “any student or other individual” (to include a respondent's threat of self-harm) and to align with FERPA's health or safety exception. Emergency removal is about addressing imminent threats, not resolving the underlying allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individualized safety and risk analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must base an emergency removal on an individualized safety and risk analysis—not on generalized, hypothetical, or speculative beliefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The analysis must examine circumstances “arising from the allegations of sexual harassment” and may include factors such as alleged violence or a respondent's threat of self-harm. The analysis cannot be based on general assumptions about sex or profiling. The recipient bears the burden to demonstrate that the removal meets the specified threshold, and must provide individualized reasons to allow the respondent to challenge the decision. The regulation leaves flexibility as to who conducts the analysis (e.g., trained employees, interdisciplinary threat assessment teams).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with disability laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must comply with applicable disability laws (IDEA, Section 504, ADA) when making emergency removal decisions for respondents, complainants, or other involved individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must avoid implicit bias or stereotype-based different treatment of students with disabilities. The presence of disability law obligations may justify different treatment (e.g., involvement of an IEP team), and an emergency removal may be constrained if the threat is a manifestation of a disability under IDEA. Training on obligations under Title IX and disability laws is permissible and encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to challenge immediately after removal
rubrics_metrics.description: When an emergency removal is used, the recipient must provide the removed individual with notice and an opportunity to challenge the removal immediately after the removal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Immediately’ is fact-specific and generally understood as occurring without delay—as soon as possible given the circumstances—but does not mean an absolute exclusion of any time interval (it need not be measured in minutes). The Department declined to prescribe specific procedures or timeframes for the post-removal challenge, leaving recipients flexibility in how to provide notice and an opportunity to be heard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'immediately' vs 'reasonably prompt'
rubrics_metrics.description: The post-removal challenge must be provided 'immediately' which is distinct from and typically more urgent than the 'reasonably prompt' timeframes governing §106.45 grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Immediately' suggests a more pressing time frame (without undue delay) to balance the respondent's due process interest against the need to address an emergency; it does not equate to the 'prompt' timeframes in §106.45 and does not require prescribing an exact minute/hour deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: No fixed time limit on length of emergency removal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declined to impose a specific temporal limitation (e.g., seven days) on how long an emergency removal may last.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should periodically assess whether an immediate threat continues or has dissipated. The grievance process is designed to conclude promptly, and emergency removal is only appropriate when necessary to address an imminent threat arising from allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures must not be punitive or disciplinary
rubrics_metrics.description: Supportive measures (per §106.30) must not be punitive or disciplinary, although they may burden a respondent so long as the burden is not unreasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include mutual or unilateral no-contact orders, re-arranging class schedules, or changing seating assignments. Whether a measure 'unreasonably burdens' a respondent is fact-specific and should be evaluated in light of the nature and purpose of the benefits/opportunities the respondent would forgo. Supportive measures offer many non-punitive options to protect complainants without imposing disciplinary sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between supportive measures and disciplinary sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may not impose disciplinary sanctions or other non-supportive measures on a respondent without following the §106.45 grievance process; emergency removal under §106.44(c) is a narrow exception to that rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency removal is intended to address immediate threats, not to serve as an interim punishment (suspension/expulsion) in lieu of the grievance process. Administrative leave and properly executed emergency removals are limited exceptions explicitly recognized by the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial vs whole-program removal discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients have discretion to remove a respondent from all or part of the recipient's education programs or activities when standards for emergency removal are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department allows narrowing a removal to certain classes, teams, clubs, living spaces, or activities. It declined to add language 'or any part thereof' but clarified that authority to exclude entirely includes lesser authority to exclude partially. Whether a partial action qualifies as a supportive measure or requires emergency removal depends on whether it is punitive/unreasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range and tailoring of supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer supportive measures to complainants (and may offer to respondents) tailored to preserve equal educational access and protect safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should carefully consider specific facts and circumstances to craft appropriate measures—examples include alternate assignments, schedule changes, no-contact orders, counseling, monitoring by staff, and reassessment/adjustment of measures if circumstances change. Alternatives should be reasonably available and not unreasonably burden the respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of threat assessment teams and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may convene threat assessment teams or train employees to conduct individualized safety and risk analyses, but use of such teams does not eliminate the requirement to provide post-removal notice and opportunity to challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department recognizes resource and capacity concerns but leaves flexibility for recipients to decide how to conduct analyses. Threat assessment teams can be used when feasible; recipients may need to provide specialized training or rely on interdisciplinary teams to perform proper assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on basing risk analysis on profiling or group characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: The safety and risk analysis cannot be based on general assumptions about sex or research/statistics that profile characteristics of alleged perpetrators; it must be individualized to the respondent and circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While factors like alleged violence, reporting delays, or police reports may be considered, the decision must address the specific facts 'arising from the allegations of sexual harassment' and avoid reliance on stereotypes or broad statistical generalizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof/demonstration for removal decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must be able to demonstrate—based on a factual, individualized safety and risk analysis—that the emergency removal meets the regulatory threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural due process and fundamental fairness require that respondents be given individualized reasons so they can meaningfully challenge the removal. Decisions should not be arbitrary; documentation of the analysis supports both defensibility and the respondent's ability to contest the basis for removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of bias and conflicts of interest in emergency removal proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency removal proceedings must be impartial, without bias or conflicts of interest, including with respect to students with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should take care to ensure impartial decision-making and may provide training to employees (including Title IX personnel) on obligations under Title IX and disability laws to prevent implicit bias influencing emergency removal decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-removal procedural scope is limited to notice and opportunity to be heard
rubrics_metrics.description: The post-removal challenge requirement guarantees notice and an opportunity to be heard immediately after removal, but does not prescribe full grievance-process protections (e.g., the full §106.45 investigation/adjudication procedures) during that immediate challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters requested full evidentiary rights and cross-examination during emergency removal challenges, but the Department declined to require detailed procedural protections for the immediate post-removal challenge, opting to ensure essential due process (notice and chance to be heard) while leaving procedural specifics to recipient discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient flexibility preserved in procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department deliberately declined to prescribe detailed procedures or narrow timeframes for the post-removal challenge and for how to conduct individualized analyses, preserving recipients' flexibility to use procedures they deem most appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This flexibility is balanced by the substantive requirements (immediate threat threshold, individualized analysis, notice/opportunity to challenge, compliance with disability laws, and the prohibition on imposing disciplinary sanctions without §106.45). Recipients remain responsible for ensuring fairness and legal compliance.
